problem: Visual (RGB-only) navigation policies lack explicit geometry and are trained on real/synthetic data that is mostly spacious and front-view only, rarely covering hazardous cases such as narrow gaps, thin obstacles and dynamic pedestrians. Sim-to-real gaps also remain large.
motivation: Real-world collection of collision-avoidance data is costly and risky, while rule-based simulation of it is nontrivial. Privileged-depth RL experts can cheaply produce hard-scenario supervision, and real-world VQA co-training may bridge the sim-to-real visual gap for a large VLA.
key_idea: Distill three capability-specific privileged-depth RL experts (reaching, squeezing, avoiding) into a 7B multi-view RGB VLA that outputs continuous velocity, using DAgger-style iterations with capability-balanced data ratios and co-training on real-world VQA.
insight: Mixing capabilities is synergistic: the Mixed-VLA gets 80/71/68 SR on reaching/squeezing/avoiding, beating every single-expert VLA and even the specialized RL teachers, whereas a Mixed-RL expert is compromised (45/58/42). VQA co-training is critical for generalization: removing it drops InternVLA-N1 S1 SR by more than 20 points on Home/Commercial, and the latent gap-axis distance between sim and real falls from 1.86 to 0.38 as VQA increases. Balanced aggregation speeds up and stabilizes convergence by emphasizing the lagging squeezing skill.
method: Capability-specific RL experts: three PPO policies in IsaacLab (static clutter reaching, dense pillars/narrow gaps squeezing, moving obstacles at 0.5-1.5 m/s avoiding) using four-view depth with ResNet-18, history token and MLP, outputting omnidirectional velocity; reward coefficients differ per skill.

Multi-view VLA student: NaVid-style video VLA extended to four RGB views (F/R/B/L), SigLIP + 2-layer MLP projector, 8-frame window, 16 fine tokens for the latest frame and 4 coarse tokens for history, Qwen2-7B LLM, action head (2-layer MLP) regressing [vx, vy, vyaw]; ~7 Hz.
Point goal as text + VQA co-training: the goal is written as a text prompt so navigation can be co-trained with real-world VQA (LongVU subset); loss L = 5*MSE(action) + CE(QA).
Initial offline distillation: 500k steps of successful expert trajectories (camera height 0.4-0.5 m, FOV 100-140° randomized) plus 100k VQA samples.

Capability-balanced DAgger: the student is deployed in the three scenes, the RL teacher labels its actions, and the data ratio p ∝ g^0.3, where g is the relative weighted-travel-time gap to the expert (+0.1). Each iteration adds 200k steps plus 40k VQA; four iterations until convergence.
Deployment: Unitree Go2 with four fisheye cameras undistorted to perspective, VLA on a remote RTX 5090 server, velocity commands sent back at ~7 Hz.

setting.backbone: SigLIP + Qwen2-7B VLA with MLP action head (fine-tuned); ResNet-18 + MLP PPO RL teachers
setting.training_data: 1.5M total expert demonstration steps from three RL experts in IsaacLab (500k initial + 4 iterations x 200k online DAgger) plus about 300k real-world VQA samples (100k initial + 40k per iteration)
setting.observation: four-view 360° RGB (front/right/back/left), 8-frame history, relative point goal as text
setting.simulator: IsaacLab (training and custom benchmark); InternVLA-N1 S1 benchmark (InternScenes, Dingo robot)
setting.privileged: none at test time (privileged depth only used by RL teachers during training)

numbers.extra: RGB only; trained on IsaacLab synthetic data + VQA, evaluated in unseen sim
numbers.evidence: Table 1 (Results in InternVLA-N1 System-1 point-goal benchmark), Home column

numbers.extra: custom scene similar in type to training

numbers_note: Real-world SR ablation (with/without VQA, 20 trials per scenario) is only given in a figure. The InternVLA-N1 S1 and IsaacLab custom benchmarks are not among the canonical benchmark names, so 'test' is used as the split label. Iteration curves are also figure-only.
results: On the InternVLA-N1 S1 point-goal benchmark, MM-Nav (RGB only) reaches SR 86.3/89.9 (Home/Commercial), beating the best baseline, SIDP (63.2/81.2 SR, using RGB-D), and the abstract claims 88.1% average SR. On the custom IsaacLab scenes it also beats NavDP, ViPlanner and iPlanner in SR and CR (e.g. squeezing 71 vs 18 for NavDP), and it outperforms its own RL teachers.
limitations: The RL experts and the sim environments have a domain gap (the Mixed-RL expert performs poorly on the InternVLA-N1 benchmark), so the approach relies on VQA co-training for generalization.
A 7B VLA needs an off-board GPU server (RTX 5090) and runs at only ~7 Hz.
Robot abstracted as a cuboid and only a point-goal task; cross-embodiment is future work; Mixed scene SR is only 47%.
